prerequisites: Basic knowledge of digital system design concepts.

learning_outcomes.text: Understanding the basics of microcontroller-based systems, special-purpose systems and the related development techniques.
Developing the capability of analyzing, designing and optimizing a microcontroller-based system, understanding the concepts and techniques for design and programming microcontrollers.
Develop the ability to properly use CAD/EDA tools for programming, designing and prototyping microcontroller systems.
Technical language of microcontroller system design.
Integrating information provided by different parties, reading and understanding commercial datasheets of industrial products.

syllabus_topics: The basics of hardware/software design for microcontroller systems
teaching_methods: Lab sessions with simulators and development boards
assessment_rules: The knowledge of the course topics will be verified, and the skills acquired during lab sessions will be evaluated. The student will have to master the techniques learned during lab experiments. Related skills will be verified through an adequately commented presentation of the lab results. The minimum requirement for passing is the understanding of the practical and technical aspects of the course, related to the operation of the systems and components discussed. The grade is assigned based on the language proficiency used to convey the discussed concepts, the ability to comprehend cause-and-effect mechanisms between design choices and performance, and the coherence and detail of the presentation of the topics.
bibliography: David A. Patterson and John L. Hennessy - "Computer Organization and Design: The Hardware/Software Interface"
institution: Università Degli Studi Di Cagliari — Ingegneria Elettronica, Informatica e delle Telecomunicazioni
